newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins firm with Bradys, IMF hopes.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins firm with Bradys, IMF hopes.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed on Wednesday after Tuesday's recovery in U.S. Treasuries and Brady bonds, dealers said.
They added the market took heart as the head of the International Monetary Fund, Michel Camdessus, said on Wednesday it was time for the fund to resume lending to Russia to back its economic reforms.
"The market looks better after yesterday's rise of Treasuries and Bradys, as well as on Camdessus's words. The market is generally optimistic," Mosbiznesbank dealer Igor Potapov said.
He added the seventh tranche, usually illiquid, was traded very actively today.
But a Deutsche Morgan Grenfell dealer said today's rise could be short-term as the market remained dependent on the U.S. economy.

"People will get rid of the long (MinFin) positions they are having as soon as the situation gets worse in the U.S. Something could happen on Friday once we see (U.S. unemployment and payroll) figures," he said.
